question.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-{z}^{2}-1}^{-z}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{-2}^{p}{\int }_{q}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{r}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$
question.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(y,z)}^{{u}_{4}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,-{z}^{2}-1\le y\le -z,\,\,0\le x\le 2y+z\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-{z}^{2}-1}^{-z}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/59e5dae7cb1d621213f3e4ef792623bdfd9a42aef19c75f7ca9d65b3af32eeda.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,-{z}^{2}-1\le y\le -z\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/9c968af98710367752a9d788b9b4c00d8c04e31d5494f7887ea5d2d635312338.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ are

$\,$ $z=\sqrt{-y-1}\,$ and $\,z=1.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ are

$\,$ $z=0\,$ and $\,z=-y.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le -1,\,\sqrt{-y-1}\le z\le 1\}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(y,z)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,0\le z\le -y\}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}{\int }_{\sqrt{-y-1}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{-y}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
